subject: Dedicated pool oscillation — root cause update and customer sync
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidretail.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Sustained slowdowns + autoscale failures (regional dedicated pool)

Hi Neha,

We started seeing a steady increase in inference latency on our dedicated pool for the US-west region beginning around 06:30 UTC this morning. By 07:15 UTC several of our user-facing endpoints reported 5–10x latency and a handful of 503s. Our ops page shows autoscale attempts but the pool didn't recover capacity; requests were queued for long periods.

This is impacting our checkout-preview feature (high QPS). Can you confirm whether this is an ongoing platform issue or something on our side? We need an ETA for stabilization and would like to schedule a short call with your on-call team.

Attaching a short export from our side with timestamps.

Thanks,
Samira
Head of Engineering, OrchidRetail

From: Connor O'brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 27 Aug 2028 13:05:00 -0000
Subject: Internal: Investigation notes — US-west dedicated pool oscillation

Team,

Summary of what I can confirm so far from the node and scheduler logs:
- 06:25 UTC: sudden spike in short-lived high-concurrency jobs (burst from OrchidRetail), ~3x expected.
- 06:30–07:00 UTC: allocator backlog grew; our placement controller retried node assignments repeatedly.
- 06:45 UTC: autoscaler executed scale-up but observed node startup failures (NV driver handshake failed intermittently for 4 nodes).
- 07:10 UTC: allocator entered repeated requeue loop because of partial node health reports. The scheduler marked nodes as available but the runtime rejected sessions due to incomplete driver initialization.

Root cause (prelim): a combination of a driver/firmware regression triggered by concurrent warmup behavior and the autoscaler not failing fast on repeated initialization failures, which caused the allocation backlog to oscillate instead of falling back to reserve capacity.

Mitigations performed (live):
- Manual cordon of the 4 nodes with failed handshakes to prevent further retries (06:58 UTC).
- Forced warm standby activation for OrchidRetail's reserved pool to drain queued requests to warm instances (07:05 UTC).
- Rolling restart of affected node images after driver rollback to the previous validated build (07:32 UTC).

Impact: sustained higher-than-SLO latency for ~40 minutes and ~1.2M token-equivalent additional cost due to extra warm standby usage and retry cycles.

Attached: ops_timeline.csv (timeline of key events and node ids). I'll follow with a draft postmortem and recommended code/ops changes.

Connor
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: ops_timeline.csv
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidretail.com>, Jamal Ortiz <jamal.ortiz@orchidretail.com>
Cc: Connor O'brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 16:30:00 -0000
Subject: US-west dedicated pool incident — preliminary root cause and next steps

Hi Samira and Jamal,

Thank you again for raising this quickly and for staying patient while we triaged. Below is a concise summary of findings, what we did to stabilize, and next steps. Connor's team is finalizing the postmortem and we'll share the full doc shortly.

What happened (brief):
- Between 06:25–07:10 UTC on 27 Aug, the US-west dedicated GPU pool servicing OrchidRetail experienced an allocation backlog and repeated scheduler retries after a spike in short-lived high-concurrency jobs from your environment.
- During scale-up attempts, 4 newly provisioned nodes intermittently failed the GPU driver handshake due to a recent driver/firmware regression combined with concurrent warmup behavior. This caused the autoscaler to continuously retry allocations instead of falling back to warm standby capacity immediately.

Immediate mitigations we executed:
- We cordoned the 4 unhealthy nodes and restarted them on the validated driver build (07:32 UTC).
- We activated warm standby for your reserved capacity so queued requests were routed to healthy instances (07:05 UTC) and the queue drained by 07:40 UTC.
- We implemented a temporary autoscaler safeguard: if a node fails initialization 3 times in 10 minutes it will be quarantined and we fail-over to warm standby in the short term.

Customer impact:
- Duration: ~06:25–07:40 UTC (peak impact ~40 minutes).
- Symptoms: elevated latency (up to 10x) and intermittent 503s during peak.
- Cost: we estimate ~1.2M token-equivalent additional cost from retries and standby activation.

Next steps (short and medium term):
- Within 48 hours: full postmortem (root cause, timeline, proposed code changes and infra mitigations). Draft link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cPostMortemDraft
- Within 2 weeks: autoscaler change to detect repeated node init failures and trigger immediate warm-standby failover; change scheduled with Karthik's team.
- Within 4 weeks: validation runs across warmup patterns and driver images to prevent regression recurrence.

Credits/compensation:
- We're offering a one-time platform credit equivalent to 50% of the incremental extra cost we identified (our current estimate: credit to cover ~600k token-equivalent). We'll finalize this in the postmortem and reflect in your upcoming invoice unless you'd prefer a different arrangement.

Attachments: initial_postmortem.pdf (summary)

Would you like to keep the 11:00 UTC slot tomorrow for a 30-min review call? We can walk the timeline and planned fixes.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll be doing everything to prevent this repeat.

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 11:00:00 -0000
Subject: Final postmortem and remediation plan — US-west dedicated pool incident (27 Aug)

Hi Samira / Jamal,

Please find attached the final postmortem slide deck and remediation plan. Key points below:

- Confirmed root cause: driver/firmware regression interacting with concurrent warmup logic, which exposed a gap in our autoscaler's failure handling.
- Corrective actions completed: driver rollback and node restarts (27 Aug), autoscaler fail-fast patch deployed to canary (28 Aug), warm standby policy tightened for reserved pools (28 Aug).
- Planned engineering changes: autoscaler quarantine threshold (2 weeks), expanded image-validation matrix (4 weeks), and a telemetry alert for repeated init failures linked to customer SLO dashboards (1 week).
- Compensation: credit for ~600k token-equivalent applied to your account; billing team will post the adjustment by Sep 5.

Attachments: final_postmortem_slide_deck.pdf
Related link: HubSpot:HS-789234 (incident record)

If useful, we can run a short technical session with your infra team to walk the failure traces — propose Thu 30 Aug 09:00 UTC. Please confirm a time that works for you.

Thanks for your partnership — we know outages are painful and appreciate your collaboration during the remediation.

Best,
Marissa Cole
